slides.title: ViTaR: Visuo-Tactile Residual Adaptation for Foundation VLA Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE RESIDUAL ADAPTATION FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: ViTaR introduces a method to modulate frozen VLA models using tactile feedback for contact-rich manipulation, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics- and force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: ViTaR enhances frozen VLA models for contact-rich tasks using tactile-guided bounded residual action corrections.
card.key_idea: It uses Effect-Guided Modeling to rank residual corrections via pairwise preferences and Residual Action Modulation to select and scale these corrections based on real-time visuo-tactile feedback.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC (61.3% avg success) and physical robots (48.3% avg success), significantly outperforming frozen OpenVLA-OFT and tactile-fusion baselines.
card.limitation: Absolute performance is constrained by the frozen base policy's semantic action quality; physical results provide limited transfer evidence.

slides.title: ForceU-VLA: A Force-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Ultrasound Scanning
slides.tldr: FORCE-AWARE VLA MODEL FOR ULTRASOUND SCANNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces ForceU-VLA, which integrates force signals and ultrasound image feedback to improve contact stability and probe pressure regulation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction through the use of multimodal feedback for precise physical interaction.

card.one_liner: ForceU-VLA enables autonomous ultrasound scanning by synergistically fusing force signals and ultrasound image feedback.
card.key_idea: A VLA framework using a Force-Ultrasound Synergistic Fusion Module (FUSFM) and a Stage-Adaptive Modulation Mechanism (SAMM) to dynamically adjust multimodal features based on contact force.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ForceU-VLA-Data (450 expert trajectories) across five clinical tasks; achieved 93.3% average success rate, outperforming $\pi_0$ and ForceVLA baselines.

slides.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a dataset and benchmark for visuo-tactile interaction with deformable objects, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of physical states.

card.one_liner: SoftVTBench is a visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for evaluating deformation-aware deformable-object manipulation.
card.key_idea: It pairs policy-visible visuo-tactile streams with hidden FEM-based physical states to measure the Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR) via object-specific calibration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Diffusion Policy, π0.5, and FastWAM on 4,000 demonstrations across 40 tasks; results show task success often masks excessive deformation.
card.limitation: The deformation tolerance is an operational simulation criterion, not a real-world material-failure or damage threshold.

slides.title: US-VLA: An Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Abdominal Scanning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a vision-language-action model for automated ultrasound probe manipulation, contributing to the study of embodied AI and real-time feedback systems relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: US-VLA enables automated abdominal ultrasound scanning by integrating clinical goals with real-time ultrasound feedback.
card.key_idea: A VLA framework using a pre-trained VLM, a USFM ultrasound encoder, and an ultrasound-aware expert fusion module to generate sequential probe manipulation actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on US-VLA-Data (liver/kidney tasks) across three subjects. Achieved 84% average success rate, outperforming pi0 baselines in success and efficiency.
card.limitation: Currently limited to specific abdominal organs; lacks additional sensory feedback like force information for enhanced physical interaction awareness.

slides.title: Vision-Based Tactile Intelligence for Robotics: Sensing, Learning, and Embodied Manipulation
slides.highlight: This review examines the integration of vision-based tactile sensors, learning methods, and simulation to improve robotic perception in contact-rich tasks, supporting RwB's focus on embodied interaction.

card.one_liner: A comprehensive review of vision-based tactile sensors (VBTSs), integrating hardware design, AI learning, and simulation.
card.key_idea: Frames VBTSs as an integrated pipeline, categorizing hardware by elastomer, shape, and optics, while mapping learning methods from low-level signal processing to tactile foundation models.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text is a survey paper reviewing existing literature rather than presenting a new experimental evaluation.
card.limitation: No single universal architecture exists; hardware must be co-designed with specific tasks, balancing resolution, compactness, and coverage.

slides.title: ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning
slides.highlight: This system utilizes vibrotactile feedback and multi-modal demonstration collection to improve success rates in contact-critical tasks, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating and improving human proficiency through physics-based and tactile feedback.

card.one_liner: ViHaTeleop is a low-cost, lightweight visual-haptic system improving success rates in contact-critical dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines SLAM-based wrist tracking, fisheye hand tracking, and LRA vibrotactile feedback with a tactile-aware retargeting constraint to ensure parallel fingertip alignment for better sensing.
card.evaluation: User study (9 participants, 6 tasks) showed success rate gains (+2.2 to +15.6%). Visual-tactile policies outperformed vision-only policies (24% vs 16% average success).
card.limitation: Small user sample (n=9), lack of external ground-truth tracking benchmarks, and limited training data for imitation learning policies.

slides.title: ReForce: Learning Force-aware Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: ReForce improves contact engagement in dexterous manipulation by predicting force residuals, supporting the multimodal perception of physical interactions relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: ReForce adapts kinematically retargeted human demonstrations using online force feedback to improve dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop force tracker trained on large-scale simulated hand-object interactions that predicts joint-command residuals to match intended contact forces without requiring digital twins.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-world tasks (paper-cup grasping, tongs) against replay and admittance control; showed lower force-tracking error and better contact engagement.
card.limitation: Relies on joint-state history without visual observations and only utilizes normal fingertip forces, ignoring shear and slip.

slides.title: EgoTac: In-the-wild Tactile Prediction from Egocentric Vision
slides.highlight: EgoTac predicts tactile information and force measurements from egocentric human videos, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills via ego-exo views and physics-based sensing.

card.one_liner: EgoTac predicts dense tactile force and contact from egocentric human videos using a large-scale dataset.
card.key_idea: A vision encoder-decoder architecture trained on 5.7M MANO-aligned image-tactile pairs, jointly regressing continuous force and classifying binary contact via AdaLN-modulated tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on in-domain splits (MAE_act < 0.06N) and OOD benchmarks (OAKINK2, FPHA, OpenTouch), consistently outperforming SOTA contact estimators.
card.limitation: OOD force evaluation requires normalized relative dynamics due to lack of cross-sensor physical calibration for absolute Newton values.
